answer: A reputation bond makes each identity costly to fake: an agent must lock a stake and build a verifiable work history before it can transact, so a Sybil farm cannot mint a thousand fresh faces for free. Think of identity as a trellis - trust climbs it slowly, one attested deed at a time, and a single quill stroke of fraud stains the whole record. Old credentials become a relic, not a shortcut: past work is checked against on-chain receipts, so an attacker must pay the full price of a real history for every fake they create.
